questions.prompt: Which ancient people built the pyramids at Giza?
questions.hint: They lived along the Nile.
questions.explanation: The pyramids at Giza were built by ancient Egyptians as tombs for their pharaohs, about 4,500 years ago.

questions.prompt: In which ancient city-state did democracy begin?
questions.hint: It is the capital of modern Greece.
questions.explanation: Athens developed the first known democracy in the 500s BCE, where citizens voted directly on laws.

questions.prompt: Which river was the center of ancient Egyptian life?
questions.hint: It flows north into the Mediterranean Sea.
questions.explanation: The yearly flood of the Nile made the land fertile and fed Egyptian civilization.

questions.prompt: Who was the first emperor of Rome?
questions.hint: He was Julius Caesar's adopted heir.
questions.explanation: Augustus became the first Roman emperor in 27 BCE. Julius Caesar was a dictator, not an emperor.

questions.prompt: Which writing system was invented in ancient Mesopotamia?
questions.hint: Scribes pressed wedge shapes into wet clay.
questions.explanation: The Sumerians created cuneiform around 3400 BCE, one of the earliest writing systems.

questions.prompt: Which kingdom did Alexander the Great rule before he conquered Persia?
questions.hint: It lay north of Greece.
questions.explanation: Alexander inherited the kingdom of Macedonia from his father Philip II and built a huge empire.

questions.prompt: Why was the Rosetta Stone so important for historians?
questions.hint: It repeats one text in three scripts.
questions.explanation: The same decree is written in Greek, Demotic and hieroglyphs, which let scholars read Egyptian hieroglyphs.

questions.prompt: The Code of Hammurabi is famous as one of the earliest...
questions.hint: It was carved on a tall stone pillar.
questions.explanation: King Hammurabi of Babylon had about 280 laws written on a stele around 1754 BCE.

questions.prompt: The ancient Egyptians built pyramids as tombs for their pharaohs.
questions.hint: Pharaohs were buried with treasures.
questions.explanation: Pyramids were royal tombs designed to protect the pharaoh in the afterlife.

questions.prompt: The ancient Olympic Games began in Greece.
questions.hint: The modern Games are named after a place in that country.
questions.explanation: The first recorded ancient Olympics were held at Olympia, Greece, in 776 BCE.

questions.prompt: Julius Caesar was the first emperor of Rome.
questions.hint: Think about his adopted heir.
questions.explanation: Caesar was a dictator. His heir Augustus became the first emperor.

questions.prompt: Cleopatra lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the building of the Great Pyramid.
questions.hint: Count the years in both directions.
questions.explanation: The Great Pyramid is about 4,500 years old. Cleopatra died in 30 BCE, around 2,000 years before 1969.

questions.prompt: Rome's empire began in 27 BCE. The western half fell in 476 CE. How long was that?

steps.why: BCE years count backward to year 1.
The calendar goes from 1 BCE to 1 CE.

questions.hint: There is no year 0 between BCE and CE.
questions.explanation: 27 BCE to 476 CE is 27 + 476 − 1 = 502 years, so about 500 years.

questions.prompt: Put these events in order, earliest first.
questions.hint: Two events are BCE before the Greek ones.
questions.explanation: The Giza pyramids (about 2500 BCE), first Olympics (776 BCE), Alexander's conquests (334–323 BCE) and the fall of Western Rome (476 CE).

questions.prompt: Which empire had its capital at Constantinople until 1453?
questions.hint: It was the eastern half of the old Roman Empire.
questions.explanation: The Byzantine Empire continued the Roman Empire in the east until the Ottomans captured Constantinople in 1453.

questions.prompt: What was the main job of a knight in medieval Europe?
questions.hint: Knights wore armor and rode horses.
questions.explanation: Knights were mounted warriors who served a lord and received land in return.

questions.prompt: Which deadly plague killed millions of people in Europe in the 1300s?
questions.hint: It spread along trade routes, carried by fleas on rats.
questions.explanation: The Black Death reached Europe in 1347 and killed perhaps a third of its people.

questions.prompt: Which system gave land to nobles in return for loyalty and military service?
questions.hint: Kings, lords, knights and peasants formed a pyramid.
questions.explanation: In feudalism a king gave land to lords, who gave land to knights, who were protected by their loyalty.

questions.prompt: Which document, sealed in 1215, limited the power of the English king?
questions.hint: Its name means Great Charter in Latin.
questions.explanation: King John was forced by his barons to accept Magna Carta, which said even the king must obey the law.

questions.prompt: Who founded the Mongol Empire in 1206?
questions.hint: His grandson Kublai later ruled China.
questions.explanation: Temujin was named Genghis Khan in 1206 and united the Mongol tribes into a vast empire.

questions.prompt: The Hundred Years' War was fought between which two kingdoms?
questions.hint: The English kings claimed the French crown.
questions.explanation: From 1337 to 1453 England and France fought over who should rule France.

questions.prompt: Whose book The Canon of Medicine was used in European universities for centuries?
questions.hint: He was a Persian scholar from around the year 1000.
questions.explanation: Ibn Sina, known as Avicenna, wrote The Canon of Medicine in the early 1000s. It was a standard text in Europe until the 1600s.

questions.prompt: Most medieval peasants owned large farms.
questions.hint: Peasants worked land for a lord.
questions.explanation: Most peasants worked small plots and farmed the lord's land in return for protection.

questions.prompt: The Black Death reached Europe in the 14th century.
questions.hint: The 14th century covers the 1300s.
questions.explanation: The plague arrived in Europe in 1347 and swept across the continent within a few years.

questions.prompt: Magna Carta was agreed by King John of England.
questions.hint: He was Richard the Lionheart's brother.
questions.explanation: King John accepted Magna Carta at Runnymede in 1215 under pressure from his barons.

questions.prompt: The Hundred Years' War lasted exactly 100 years.
questions.hint: Check the start and end dates: 1337 and 1453.
questions.explanation: The conflict ran from 1337 to 1453, which is 116 years. The name is only a rough description.

questions.prompt: How many years passed between the Norman conquest (1066) and Magna Carta (1215)?
questions.hint: Take the earlier date from the later date.
questions.explanation: 1215 − 1066 = 149, so Magna Carta came 149 years after the Norman conquest.

questions.prompt: Put these events in order, earliest first.
questions.hint: The dates run from 800 to the 1300s.
questions.explanation: Charlemagne was crowned in 800, the Normans conquered England in 1066, Magna Carta came in 1215 and the Black Death arrived in 1347.

questions.prompt: Put these events in order, earliest first.
questions.hint: Two are in the 1700s and two are in the 1900s.
questions.explanation: US Declaration of Independence 1776, French Revolution 1789, World War I 1914, Indian independence 1947.

questions.prompt: In which year did World War II end?
questions.hint: It was the middle of the 1940s.
questions.explanation: World War II ended in 1945, with Germany surrendering in May and Japan in August and September.

questions.prompt: Which country was the birthplace of the Industrial Revolution?
questions.hint: Factories, coal and steam appeared there in the 1700s.
questions.explanation: The Industrial Revolution began in Britain in the late 1700s, with textile mills and steam power.

questions.prompt: Which war was fought from 1914 to 1918?
questions.hint: It was once called the Great War.
questions.explanation: World War I lasted from 1914 to 1918 and involved most of the great powers.

questions.prompt: Which event of July 1789 is seen as the start of the French Revolution?
questions.hint: Crowds attacked a royal prison in Paris.
questions.explanation: On 14 July 1789 a crowd stormed the Bastille. The king was executed later, in 1793.

questions.prompt: Who is credited with patenting the first practical telephone in 1876?
questions.hint: He was born in Scotland.
questions.explanation: Alexander Graham Bell received the first US telephone patent in 1876.

questions.prompt: Which treaty of 1919 formally ended World War I with Germany?
questions.hint: It was signed in a palace near Paris.
questions.explanation: The Treaty of Versailles was signed in June 1919 and placed heavy terms on Germany.

questions.prompt: Which party took power in Russia in the October Revolution of 1917?
questions.hint: Their leader was Lenin.
questions.explanation: The Bolsheviks under Lenin seized power in October 1917, replacing the Provisional Government.

questions.prompt: The Berlin Conference of 1884–85 set rules for European colonization of which continent?
questions.hint: It led to the 'Scramble' for territory.
questions.explanation: European powers met in Berlin to agree how to divide and claim land in Africa, with no African leaders present.

questions.prompt: The Industrial Revolution began in Britain.
questions.hint: Think about steam engines and textile mills.
questions.explanation: Britain led the way in factories, coal, iron and steam power from the late 1700s.

questions.prompt: World War II ended in 1945.
questions.hint: It was the middle of the 1940s.
questions.explanation: The war in Europe ended in May 1945, and the war with Japan ended in September 1945.

questions.prompt: The French Revolution began before American independence was declared.
questions.hint: Compare 1776 with 1789.
questions.explanation: The Americans declared independence in 1776. The French Revolution began in 1789.

questions.prompt: The Titanic sank during World War I.
questions.hint: The war began in 1914.
questions.explanation: The Titanic sank in April 1912, two years before World War I began.

questions.prompt: Which century does the year 1789 belong to?
questions.hint: The 1st century is years 1 to 100.
questions.explanation: Century numbers round up, so 1789 is in the 18th century (1701–1800).

questions.prompt: Who was the first Prime Minister of India?
questions.hint: He served from 1947 until 1964.
questions.explanation: Jawaharlal Nehru became Prime Minister at independence in 1947. Rajendra Prasad was the first President.

questions.prompt: In which year did India become independent from British rule?
questions.hint: It was on 15 August.
questions.explanation: India became independent on 15 August 1947.

questions.prompt: Who is widely called the 'Father of the Nation' in India?
questions.hint: He led nonviolent protests such as the Salt March.
questions.explanation: Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi led the nonviolent freedom movement and is called the Father of the Nation.

questions.prompt: Which Mauryan emperor turned toward Buddhism after the Kalinga War?
questions.hint: He ruled in the 200s BCE.
questions.explanation: Ashoka was horrified by the suffering in the Kalinga War (about 261 BCE) and later promoted peace and Buddhism.

questions.prompt: Which Mughal emperor built the Taj Mahal?
questions.hint: He built it as a tomb for his wife Mumtaz Mahal.
questions.explanation: Shah Jahan ordered the Taj Mahal in Agra in memory of his wife Mumtaz Mahal. It was completed around 1653.

questions.prompt: Gandhi's Dandi March of 1930 was a protest against the British tax on what?
questions.hint: Everyone needs it in food.
questions.explanation: The 1930 march to Dandi challenged the British salt tax and monopoly and began the Civil Disobedience Movement.

questions.prompt: Which 1757 battle helped the East India Company gain control of Bengal?
questions.hint: It was fought against the Nawab of Bengal.
questions.explanation: At Plassey in 1757 Robert Clive's forces defeated Siraj ud-Daulah, the Nawab of Bengal.

questions.prompt: In which year was the Quit India Movement launched?
questions.hint: It happened during World War II.
questions.explanation: Gandhi called for 'Do or Die' and an end to British rule in August 1942.

questions.prompt: India became independent in 1947.
questions.hint: It is celebrated on 15 August.
questions.explanation: India gained independence from British rule on 15 August 1947.

questions.prompt: The Taj Mahal is in the city of Agra.
questions.hint: It stands on the Yamuna river.
questions.explanation: The Taj Mahal is in Agra, Uttar Pradesh, on the banks of the Yamuna.

questions.prompt: Rajendra Prasad was the first Prime Minister of India.
questions.hint: He held a different office.
questions.explanation: Rajendra Prasad was the first President. Jawaharlal Nehru was the first Prime Minister.

questions.prompt: Ashoka was an emperor of the Mauryan dynasty.
questions.hint: His grandfather was Chandragupta Maurya.
questions.explanation: Ashoka ruled the Mauryan Empire from about 268 to 232 BCE.

questions.prompt: How many years passed between the 1857 revolt and independence in 1947?
questions.hint: Take the earlier date from the later date.
questions.explanation: 1947 − 1857 = 90, so independence came 90 years after the 1857 revolt.

questions.prompt: Put these in order, earliest first.
questions.hint: One is thousands of years BCE.
questions.explanation: Indus Valley cities (about 2600 BCE), the Mauryan Empire (322 BCE), the Mughal Empire (1526) and independence (1947).

questions.prompt: Step only on things built by the Romans.
questions.hint: Think of Rome, not Greece or Egypt.
questions.explanation: The Romans built the Colosseum, aqueducts, roads, the Pantheon and Hadrian's Wall. The Parthenon is Greek and the Great Pyramid is Egyptian.

questions.prompt: Step only on events of the Middle Ages (about 500 to 1500).
questions.hint: Check the date of each event.
questions.explanation: Magna Carta, the Black Death, the First Crusade, the Norman conquest and Charlemagne's crowning (800) are medieval. The others happened much earlier or later.

questions.prompt: Step only on events of World War 2.
questions.hint: World War 2 lasted from 1939 to 1945.
questions.explanation: The Battle of Britain, D-Day, Pearl Harbor, Stalingrad and Midway were in World War 2. The Somme was World War 1; the others were earlier still or in between.

questions.prompt: Step only on rulers of the Mughal Empire.
questions.hint: The Mughal Empire began in 1526 with Babur.
questions.explanation: Babur, Akbar, Jahangir, Shah Jahan and Aurangzeb were Mughal emperors. Ashoka and Chandragupta were Mauryan, Shivaji was Maratha, Tipu Sultan ruled Mysore.
